Impeccable

im-PEK-uh-bul -- stress on the second syllable, PEK. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Impeccable is flawless, spotless, or faultless.

His impeccable manners impressed even the host's grandmother, who was famously hard to please.

Worked Example

A pastry chef sends out forty identical tarts: every crust the same shade of gold, every fruit slice at the same angle, not one drip on any of the forty plates.

The work is impeccable -- flawless, spotless, faultless. Impeccable is the very top grade of 'no mistakes.' It does not mean 'very good'; it means 'nothing anywhere is wrong.'

How Impeccable Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

flawless

flawless: without a single flaw

faultless

faultless: containing no faults or errors

immaculate

immaculate: perfectly clean, without a blemish

Antonyms

flawed

flawed: containing faults or errors

shoddy

shoddy: carelessly made or carelessly done

How Strong Is It? — faultless → impeccable → immaculate

faultless vs. impeccable

faultless vs. impeccable: Faultless is the plainer word and stops at 'no mistakes,' while impeccable adds polish -- a standard so high that no critic could find a single thing to fix.

immaculate vs. impeccable

immaculate vs. impeccable: Immaculate leans in the direction of cleanliness: impeccable work contains no errors, while an immaculate kitchen contains no speck of dirt -- perfection you can see on the surface.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of impeccable.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — im-

prefix — im-: not (the form in- takes before p) (Latin in-)

root — peccable

root — peccable: capable of sinning or erring (Latin peccare 'to sin, to make a mistake')

Put it together

Put it together: Impeccable is this unit's prefix in its im- form (in- shifts to im- before p) on Latin peccare ('to sin'), so the literal reading is 'not capable of sinning' -- incapable of a single fault. The honest caveat: 'peccable' is technically an English word but so rare that almost no one has seen it, which makes this split likely rather than confirmed. The root does surface in a word real people use: peccadillo, a small sin.

Use the root in a new word: peccadillo

Use the root in a new word: peccadillo: The coach forgave the peccadillo of a missed bus and let him play anyway.

Root Check

Word Choice

Impeccable is praise without reservation: impeccable timing, impeccable manners, an impeccable record, impeccable taste. Because it literally means 'incapable of sin,' it is an absolute -- something either is impeccable or it is not, and 'fairly impeccable' does not work.
